name: carousel
description: Slides on a scroll-snapping track with dots that link to each one, scrolled by the browser, with an optional module so following a dot costs no history entry.

attributes.name: data-slides
attributes.description: How many slides are visible at once.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between slides, and above the dots.

children.description: The scrolling track holding the slides. A scrolling region is an interactive one, so give it role="group", a name, and tabindex="0".
One slide each, with an id a dot can link to.
A list of links, one per slide, each named by a span carrying visually-hidden or by an aria-label. With carousel.js loaded the module scrolls the track itself, so following one adds no history entry.

markers.name: data-track
markers.description: The scrolling track that holds the slides.

markers.name: data-slide
markers.description: One slide, with an id a dot can link to.

markers.name: data-dots
markers.description: The list of links to the slides, one per slide.

tokens.name: --yeti-control-size
tokens.description: The pressable area around a dot.

tokens.name: --yeti-carousel-scroll
tokens.description: How the track scrolls when a dot is followed.

tokens.name: --yeti-duration-fast
tokens.description: How long a dot takes to grow under the pointer.

keyboard.action: Focuses the track, then each dot in turn.

a11y.notes: Label the region and give it aria-roledescription="carousel" so it is announced as one. The dots are links to slide ids, so the browser does the scrolling and the keyboard works without help; each needs a name, from a span carrying visually-hidden or from an aria-label, since a dot has no room for visible text. They jump to a slide but cannot report which slide is showing, because CSS cannot know that. Loading carousel.js keeps the back button useful by scrolling the track instead of navigating; without it the dots still work, and each one followed is one press of back. Nothing essential should live behind a slide a reader has to find. The track scrolls, so it must be reachable from the keyboard: give it role="group", an aria-label, and tabindex="0". It is a group rather than a region because the carousel itself is already the landmark.

events.name: yeti:slide
events.description: Dispatched on the .carousel when a dot scrolls the track, with the slide's zero-based index.
